THE WORK, EXPLAINED

Know what your removal includes.

Every removal starts with a different setting. A tree in an open yard presents different access and handling questions from one beside a roof, fence, driveway, or neighboring property. Photos help us understand the request, and some jobs need an onsite assessment before a final estimate.

Tell us why you are considering removal and show the tree from more than one angle. Include the base, canopy, and surrounding space. We will discuss whether the requested work can be accepted, the proposed scope, and scheduling after reviewing those details.

What affects tree removal cost in Houston?

Tree size and condition, surrounding structures, access, and the amount of material to handle influence the estimate. The quote also needs to reflect what you want done with the branches, trunk sections, and stump. A photograph starts the conversation; it does not replace an assessment when the job requires one.

Plan for the stump before the tree is gone

Tree removal and stump grinding are separate parts of the project. If you want a clearer lawn or have plans for the area, ask to include a stump grinding estimate. Confirm the grinding area, depth, and chip handling with the rest of the scope.

START WITH A PHOTO

BEFORE WE GET TO WORK

Tree removal
questions.

Can you quote removal from photos?+

Photos help us begin reviewing a job. Tree condition, overhead lines, nearby structures, and access may require an onsite assessment before a final price or acceptance of the work.

Does tree removal include stump grinding?+

Only when it is included in the agreed scope. Ask about stump grinding when requesting your removal estimate so both stages can be discussed together.

Will you haul away the trunk and branches?+

Debris handling is confirmed with the estimate. Tell us whether you want material removed or specific wood left onsite so the quote reflects your request.

How do I request a Houston tree removal estimate?+

Call or text (832) 501-9594 with your ZIP code, photos, and a description of the tree. Include nearby structures, access limitations, and your cleanup preferences.
